page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u1-c1m1.3xlarge is a general-purpose compute instance built on the KVM hypervisor and the x86_64 architecture. It provides 12 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 6 physical Intel Xeon cores running at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz with two threads per core. The hardware architecture incorporates a 33 MB L3 cache alongside support for instruction sets including AVX, AVX-512F, AES, and FMA. System memory totals 12.0 GB, yielding a 1:1 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 1.0 GB per core. The instance includes no bundled local storage, necessitating external cloud disk attachment, and provides a 4 Gbps baseline network throughput without bundled public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations indicate consistent mid-tier compute throughput across synthetic and application-level workloads. The instance achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 1426.0 and a multi-core score of 7074.0, while PassMark reports a total CPU score of 15105.88. In multi-threaded execution, stress-ng registers 11580.66, and Clang compilation reaches a score of 11712.0. Memory throughput reaches 82.64 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 53.16 GB/sec for writes. The strict 1 GB memory allocation per vCPU limits capacity during large memory operations; for instance, prompt processing throughput on a 7B language model drops to 24.11 tokens/sec, and larger 70B models cannot be loaded into system memory.

The 1:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio offers favorable cost efficiency for compute-centric workloads that do not demand extensive RAM pools. Compute density remains high, enabling efficient CPU core utilization without paying for idle memory allocations. Best-fit use cases include multi-threaded software compilation, batch processing, static web serving (measured at 13.6 GB/sec), and distributed worker nodes that stream data directly across the 4 Gbps network interface rather than holding state in local memory.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u1-c1m1.3xlarge is an x86_64 server instance powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.5 GHz. It features 12 dedicated vCPUs across 6 physical cores with hyper-threading, accompanied by 12.0 GB of system memory, yielding a dense 1:1 memory-to-vCPU allocation. The hardware platform includes AVX-512 vector instructions and a 33 MB L3 cache, backed by a 4 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Local storage is not included, requiring network-attached block storage for persistent data. In benchmark evaluations, the instance delivers balanced multi-threaded performance, recording a Geekbench multi-core score of 7074.0 and 11.77 million Redis SET operations per second. However, the 1.0 GB per vCPU ratio restricts memory-intensive tasks such as large language model inference. The instance is well suited for CPU-bound pipelines, software build clusters, batch data transformation, and horizontal microservices that maintain small individual working sets.
